page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and running on the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine provision provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, utilizing two threads per core. System memory is configured at 4.0 GB total, delivering a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is strictly network-attached as no local instance storage is included, and hardware-accelerated processing is not supported due to the absence of dedicated GPUs. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate adequate single-threaded responsiveness alongside predictable lower bounds for multi-threaded performance due to the two-vCPU ceiling. Single-core measurements show balanced throughput, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,487.0 and stress-ng single-core output reaching 1,874.59. Single-threaded gzip compression performs solidly at 27.47 GB/sec, and text processing registers an average score of 1,584.0. In contrast, multi-core metrics place the instance in the lower percentiles: PassMark CPU score is 2,939.36, Geekbench multi-core is 1,742.0, and stress-ng multi-core is 1,926.09, which reflects the constrained physical core count.

Memory bandwidth benchmarks record 14.32 GB/sec read and 12.85 GB/sec write on 256 MB uncached block tests, accompanying a PassMark memory score of 1,199.53. In-memory data throughput achieves 1.91 million Redis SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 3.33 GB/sec. Micro-scale LLM inference processing via a 135M model generates 55.21 tokens per second. Because there is no bundled local storage, storage performance is directly dependent on network block storage attachments.

The qualitative hardware balance delivers dedicated compute access on modern Intel Xeon silicon without excessive memory overhead. Suitable workloads include lightweight front-end web serving, single-threaded processing microservices, small utility background workers, and low-traffic network proxy tasks where memory footprint requirements remain strictly under 4 GB.
